Trading Notes: Great 4K capture of this lovely tour on its last day in Dallas. It's filmed in 16:9 from the far right orchestra, with a mix of wides, mediums, and closeups. There's no major obstruction other than the tops of heads that can sometimes be seen during wideshots and the sound equipment that blocks some action that takes place on the far side of stage left. There are unfortunately some extended blackouts, notably two minutes at the top of Act One, three minutes at the top of Act Two, and six minutes during the lengthy scene at Mrs. Higgins' house. There are quick dropouts that take place right after Wouldn't it be Loverly?, Alfred's bargain, shortly before Eliza's entrance at the horse race, during On the Street Where You Live, and before I've Grown Accustomed to Her Face, though these don't last long. The washout is improved from this angle though there's still some during the darker scenes. The sound is excellent. Includes playbill scans.
